clue.text: Hyperbole ever develops with speed in a watering-hole

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters and the speed unit inside the watering-hole word

parts.note: an oasis is a watering-hole in the desert

indicators.note: develops says the letters of ever change into a new form

parts.note: MPH, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: Someone notes that exaggeration grows quicker in a pub, the watering-hole of the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' rearranges ever to VERE; 'in' splits the watering-hole word around that and the speed unit. 'Hyperbole' is the definition, not part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration, putting too much stress on a point.

clue.text: Not the type to have a flutter?…

definitions.text: Not the type to have a flutter?…

parts.words: Not the type to have a flutter?…
parts.note: reads as someone who never bets, but a flutter is also a beat of the wings, and this big bird cannot fly

explanation.walkthrough: A 'flutter' is British slang for a small bet; the definition reads it as wing-flapping by a flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest bird is flightless, so it never flaps its wings in flight.

clue.text: … Grand's very good invested in City

indicators.note: invested in means one piece is put inside the other, like money placed within

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: A big investment in the City of London is praised as grand and very good.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means heroic in scale, impressive.

clue.text: Brought into play? Edward's holding King back, note

indicators.note: holding says the name's letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: ED is short for Edward

indicators.note: back means the royal word is read the other way

parts.note: REX is Latin for king
TE is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Edward keeps a king and a musical note back in some game or performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the Latin king to XER; 'holding' has Edward's short form wrap that and the note.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert a force or influence is to bring it into use.

clue.text: Chemist's stiff mixture put on edges of ulcer

parts.note: a paste is a thick, stiff mixture

indicators.note: edges of picks the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A pharmacist puts a thick ointment round the rim of a sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places PASTE above UR in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French scientist who developed pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: It's just like Lily, having a drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A woman named Lily is described as always having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Lily is a plant, not a woman; this plant is called the arum lily.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a plant with a lily-like flower spathe, often called the arum lily.

clue.text: Elected man harbouring Liberal idea

parts.note: IN means elected, as a party is in power

indicators.note: harbouring means the chess piece shelters a letter inside it

parts.note: a king is a man in chess

explanation.surface: A newly elected politician secretly holds a Liberal notion.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a faint notion or hint.

clue.text: Like tough material, only partly worsted

definitions.text: Like tough material, only partly worsted

parts.words: Like tough material, only partly worsted
parts.note: worsted is both a woollen fabric and a word for beaten; a tough character beaten only in part is knocked over but not finished

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as fabric talk; 'worsted' really means defeated, and 'tough material' is a resilient person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone defeated for now yet still able to fight back.

clue.text: Alien group likely to have a field-day?

definitions.meaning: in cricket the team that is out does the fielding all day

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'in' and the fielding side is 'out', so an out side spends the day in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or external; a side that is out in cricket is the one fielding.

clue.text: Attached? Infatuated

definitions.meaning: attached means fixed in place with glue

explanation.definitionFit: Glued on means physically attached; being keen on someone is slang for being besotted.

clue.text: Secure Knight facing decline

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
to ail is to decline in health

explanation.surface: A knight confronts his own decline with resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fasten it firmly, making it secure.

clue.text: Further dam, mile off

indicators.note: off means the abbreviation is taken away from the word

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.walkthrough: 'dam' is the river barrier in the surface; here it is a mother animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean additional, further, as in other reasons.

clue.text: Put up tent's second stay

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Campers pitch their second tent and stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: To bide is to remain or wait, as in biding one's time.

clue.text: Sap's dead wet

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Tree sap is described as dead wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap someone's strength is to exhaust it, to draw it away.

clue.text: One set, in spirit

parts.note: an means one, as in an apple
to gel is to set like a jelly

explanation.surface: Someone sets about something in good spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a heavenly spirit.

clue.text: Escorted old lady in

indicators.note: in places the woman word inside the second-hand word

parts.note: used means old, second-hand
her is a lady, a female pronoun

explanation.definitionFit: Ushered means guided or shown the way, as at a theatre.

clue.text: Revoke? American's taken aback, in game, by East

indicators.note: in means the reversed name sits inside the abbreviated game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: taken aback says the name is read from its end

parts.note: Gene is taken as a typical American man's name

explanation.surface: A card player cries foul when an American opponent is surprised during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' gives ENEG; 'in' puts it inside the rugby abbreviation. Revoke and renegue are card-game terms for failing to follow suit; Gene stands for any American man.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, to renegue is to fail to follow suit when able, also called a revoke.

clue.text: Eating cut of meat with drink brought round

indicators.note: brought round means the drink word encloses the meat word

parts.note: nog is a drink, as in eggnog
shin is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: Someone eats a joint of meat with a drink served alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: Noshing is British slang for eating heartily.

clue.text: Pink fish

definitions.meaning: to pink is to cut cloth with a zigzag or curved edge

explanation.definitionFit: Shears give fabric a wavy decorative edge, as pinking does; the word also names a bivalve shellfish.

clue.text: Vivid Greek character clad in trimmed elegance

indicators.note: clad in says the letter is dressed in the shortened word around it
trimmed means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: grace means elegance
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

clue.text: Mild gum containing hint of lime

indicators.note: hint of takes just the first letter of the next word

explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild, gentle.

clue.text: Island-reportedly rough one, getting about

explanation.walkthrough: In British speech COARSE sounds like CORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Peer over letter, insensitive to the tone?

clue.text: Gin in one's mouth

slang for mouth, as in shut your...

clue.text: Brief, short and formal

indicators.note: short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: to prime is to brief someone

explanation.surface: A list of qualities: brief, short and formal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prim means stiffly proper and formal.

indicators.note: an attribute of means part belongs to the word, so the letters sit within it

explanation.definitionFit: A vale is a valley, a dip in the land.

parts.note: rasps are harsh croaking sounds

clue.text: Loose ulna she fractured

clue.text: Fly circling quiet study

parts.note: a fly is an insect

explanation.surface: A fly buzzes round a quiet study room.

clue.text: Sixth Form elite?

parts.note: the senior year groups of a school stand at the top, and the phrase also names society's top tier

explanation.walkthrough: The Sixth Form is the final two years of a British secondary school, its highest forms.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior forms are the school's highest years, and the phrase also means the aristocracy.
